subject: Physics
scope: Fifteen carefully scoped Year 1 Physics concept and graph interpretation mock recall cards, not a full AQA specification certification.
notes: High-priority reinforcement, including previously reported difficulties with motion graphs, projectiles, moments, internal resistance, strain and photoelectric threshold. No practical apparatus instructions.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: For a velocity–time graph crossing below the time axis, how do you calculate total distance?
cards.back: Add the magnitudes of all areas between the graph and the time axis.
accept: Add the magnitudes of all areas between the graph and the time axis.
Sum the absolute areas on both sides of the axis.
Add positive and negative regions as positive distances.
reject: Use the signed total area as the distance.
Ignore the regions below the axis.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What does the gradient of a tangent to a curved velocity–time graph represent?
accept: Instantaneous acceleration at that time.
The acceleration at the point of tangency.
Instantaneous rate of change of velocity.
reject: Total displacement since the start.
The average speed over the whole journey.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Ignoring air resistance, what happens to the horizontal velocity of a projectile during flight?
accept: It remains constant.
Horizontal velocity stays unchanged.
It has zero horizontal acceleration.
reject: It increases because of gravity.
It becomes zero at the highest point.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is the vertical acceleration of a freely moving projectile near Earth's surface?
cards.back: Approximately 9.81 m s⁻² downwards throughout its flight.
accept: Approximately 9.81 m s⁻² downwards throughout its flight.
Constant downward acceleration g.
Acceleration is g vertically downwards.
reject: It becomes zero at maximum height.
It always points in the direction of the velocity.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Why do the action and reaction forces in Newton's third law not cancel on one object?
accept: They act on different objects.
The equal and opposite forces act on separate bodies.
They form a pair on different interacting objects.
reject: They act at different times.
The forces are not equal.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What distance is used in the moment of a couple, M = Fd?
cards.back: The perpendicular separation between the two parallel forces.
accept: The perpendicular separation between the two parallel forces.
The perpendicular distance between their lines of action.
The distance between the two lines of action, measured at right angles.
reject: The entire length of either force arrow.
The distance from either force to any arbitrary origin.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What condition is required for total momentum to be conserved in a system?
cards.back: The resultant external force on the system is zero.
accept: The resultant external force on the system is zero.
There is no net external force acting on the system.
The system is isolated from resultant external forces.
reject: The objects must move at constant speed individually.
No internal forces may exist.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What does the area under a force–extension graph give during elastic loading?
cards.back: The work done stretching the material, stored as elastic strain energy if no losses occur.
accept: The work done stretching the material, stored as elastic strain energy if no losses occur.
Work done in stretching, equal to recoverable elastic energy for elastic loading.
Energy transferred by the stretching force.
reject: The Young modulus.
The tensile stress.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What does the gradient of the initial straight part of a stress–strain graph give?
accept: The Young modulus.
Young's modulus of the material.
Stress divided by strain in the elastic linear region.
reject: The extension of the wire.
The breaking force.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What distinguishes plastic deformation after a load is removed?
accept: A permanent deformation remains.
The sample does not return completely to its original shape.
Some strain persists when the force is removed.
reject: The material returns exactly to its original length.
Stress is always proportional to strain.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: For a uniform wire, how is resistance related to resistivity, length and cross-sectional area?
accept: R = ρL/A.
Resistance equals resistivity times length divided by area.
R equals rho times L over A.
reject: R = ρA/L.
R = L/(ρA).

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What does the vertical intercept on a terminal-p.d. V against current I graph represent?
accept: The emf of the cell.
The cell's electromotive force.
The voltage at zero current, equal to emf.
reject: The internal resistance.
The lost volts at maximum current.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What does the negative gradient of a cell's V–I graph represent?
accept: Minus the internal resistance, −r.
The slope is negative internal resistance.
Gradient = −r for V = ε − Ir.
reject: The emf of the cell.
The external load resistance at every point.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: If light frequency is below the threshold frequency, what does raising its intensity do to photoelectron emission?
cards.back: No photoelectrons are emitted, regardless of intensity.
accept: No photoelectrons are emitted, regardless of intensity.
Increasing intensity cannot produce photoelectrons below threshold frequency.
Emission remains absent because individual photons lack sufficient energy.
reject: More light intensity creates photoelectrons even below threshold.
Electrons are emitted only after a longer exposure.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Why do repeated readings not automatically remove a systematic measurement error?
cards.back: A consistent bias affects all the readings.
accept: A consistent bias affects all the readings.
Repeating does not correct a fixed offset or calibration bias.
Systematic error remains because it shifts measurements consistently.
reject: Repeated measurements always remove zero error.
A fixed calibration error is random scatter.
